title: Debra Hill is as Vital to the Success of "Halloween" as John Carpenter

commenti.body:
Gotta 1,000% disagree with you here

Honestly the score alone makes this a silly thing to literally argue IMO. It’s either the most or 2nd most iconic horror film score of all time (Jaws being the only remote competition whatsoever), and it’s plainly one of the most recognizable and beloved scores ever

But even past that I just disagree in general with the premise isolated to the script alone. 

Loomis and the spectre of Michael Meyers is the heart and soul of what makes Halloween great anyway

Your quote from Mark Clark to me makes no points whatsoever to support its claim that “Michael proved easy to copy but Laurie was impossible to duplicate.”

There’s really nothing memorable or notable about the teens in Halloween as opposed to similar slashers. The difference isn’t even really Laurie Strode. It’s Jamie Lee Curtis’s performance and the subtle things Carpenter does with the camera and editing (the “Don’t Fear the Reaper” Easter Egg, the cuts in the shrub scene, the winking shot of the original The Thing during the babysitting adventure, etc.).

Laure is just another Final Girl, elevated by JLC and Carpenter. Her friends are absolutely worthless and uninteresting and undifferentiated from any other slasher

Hell I’d even argue that Black Christmas has much better overall characters and dynamics with their victims, and also-predecessor slasher Texas Chainsaw Massacre likewise far outdoes Halloween with memorable characters and interesting dialogue outside its scenes of slaughter

Having rewatched it I feel Halloween is a little blunted by the overuse of the tropes of the slasher genre, and that unfortunately includes the teenage centric cast. A lot of the characters and the situations just feels like things you have seen in every slasher ever made, and so this blunts the power and horror of the original.

The only thing I grant Halloween is that the central teenage cast isn't completely moronic and horrible, which definitely became a thing for later slashers. I actually did care about the characters in Halloween, especially Laurie so it was easy to feel the tension and horror because of that.

I think the difference IS Laurie Strode, and is evident even in Halloween itself by comparing Laurie to her friends. Her friends are the common horror trope victims — unaware, single-minded (the trope is sex and that is true here as well), egoistic. Laurie is such a different character and makes such different choices than her friends or most other slasher characters, and that definitely is what sets Halloween apart narrative-wise. The camera, the way that Myers is portrayed and spoken about throughout, and the score (imo it us #1) all add to what makes Halloween unique, but Laurie definitely does too and that shouldn’t be minimized.
No, that’s just the difference in any Final Girl setup, which is what Scream later comments on. Laurie is only “different” in that she’s not fucking someone or doing drugs
What would you say is different about what Laurie does, either in relation to her friends or other slasher film characters?
